headline: The overnight chip catch-up did not survive Europe: Nvidia gives back, and metals follow it down

findings.headline: The Huang rally flipped, and a firmer Ifo could not stop it
findings.body: Asia's chip catch-up was the last leg of Monday's move: Nvidia is lower again in premarket after Monday's near-$1 trillion gain, with Micron, AMD, Marvell and the neocloud names such as CoreWeave also giving back. Germany's Ifo index rose to 90.6 from 90.1, but the gain came from services and trade while manufacturing slipped after six straight rises, so it gave Europe no reason to buck the tech fade. With Wednesday's PCE the last inflation read before a December Fed meeting that markets expect to hike, the bounce now has to prove it was more than short covering.

findings.headline: Miners lead Europe lower as copper unwinds its Nvidia bounce
findings.body: Copper's Monday jump rode the AI data-centre story, and it is unwinding with it, dragging the London miners down hardest as the market refocuses on Chinese demand and US rate hikes. ING calls this a financial-market move rather than weaker fundamentals: Chinese import premiums and nearby spreads still point to a tight physical market. That gap between paper selling and physical tightness is what would make metals the first to rebound if PCE comes in soft.

findings.headline: Tullow buys time with a Ghana tax settlement, at a cost
findings.body: Tullow agreed to pay $287.5 million over several years to settle $387 million of Ghanaian claims, and will hand Ghana the revenue from 100 billion cubic feet of Jubilee gas from 2029. It cut free cash flow guidance to $160-210 million from $170-250 million, so debt reduction gets harder with the bonds due for refinancing by the first half of 2028. Panmure keeps a sell and still flags liquidity risk before end-2027: the relief rally removes a tail risk, not the balance-sheet problem.

view: Our view: The overnight story did not hold. Monday looks like a positioning squeeze in a crowded AI trade rather than a new leg, and until PCE settles the December hike debate, chips and metals are likely to keep trading as one risk bet.
